glosses: der Logik widersprechend; den gegebenen Tatsachen nicht entsprechend

examples.text: Dass diese Überlegungen nicht ganz folgewidrig sind, sei mit Verweis auf die Realität untermauert: Die Tötung von Embryonen geschieht beispielsweise durch die Spirale millionenfach, ohne dass sie sonderlich kontrovers wäre.

translations.source_sense_description: der Logik widersprechend; den gegebenen Tatsachen nicht entsprechend

glosses: Not compatible (with another thing); incompatible, discrepant, at odds.

examples.text: His account of the evening was inconsistent with the security-camera footage.

glosses: Lacking internal consistency; self-contradicting; not compatible with itself.

examples.text: He gave an inconsistent account of the evening, saying he called her before eight, but later that he had not talked to her until after nine.
He was one of those men of inconsistent politics, governed at once by prejudice and sympathies, whose 'attitude' it is impossible to foretell.

glosses: Not consistent or coherent in thought or behavior.

examples.text:
“Take him for better or worse,” added Mr. Lee, “and I think he is the strangest and most inconsistent man I ever saw.”
“Inconsistent!” resumed Mr. Jones. “He is worse than inconsistent. Inconsistencies may be pardoned as constitutional defects [...]”

glosses: Having the property that a contradiction can be derived.

translations.source_sense_description: der Logik widersprechend; den gegebenen Tatsachen nicht entsprechend

examples.text: —Don’t mope over it all day, he said. I’m inconsequent.

glosses: illogical; not following from the premises

examples.text: She looked at him a minute, and it came to him as he met it an inconsequent sense that her eyes, when one got their full clearness, were still as beautiful as they had been in youth, only beautiful with a strange, cold light - a light that somehow was a part of the effect, if it wasn't rather a part of the cause, of the pale, hard sweetness of the season and the hour.
That possibility was now ever so much further from sight than on the eve of his arrival, and he perfectly felt that, should it come at all, it would have to be at best inconsequent and violent.
